short_description: A mouse-tracking go/no-go paradigm with a dynamic start that captures response inhibition during ongoing movement execution, evaluated for test-retest reliability of behavioral and kinematic stopping measures across two sessions.
long_description: The Mouse Tracking Go/No-Go Study develops and evaluates a continuous-response go/no-go paradigm designed to capture inhibitory control during ongoing motor execution. Participants performed a mouse-tracking task where a stimulus digit appeared in a response box only after the cursor crossed a movement-contingent threshold above a start box, ensuring that inhibitory processes are engaged during active movement rather than before movement initiation. On go trials (digits 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8), participants responded by clicking within the response box within a 1500 ms deadline. On no-go trials (digits 1, 9), participants were required to inhibit the ongoing movement and withhold any click. Successful stopping on no-go trials was operationalized using a velocity-threshold method (speed dropping below 10 px/s for 150 ms, with a sustained stopping verification). The study employed a 2 (session) × 2 (trial type: go, no-go) repeated-measures within-subjects design. Twenty-six participants completed the task in two sessions separated by approximately one week; two participants were absent from session 2 and were excluded from reliability analyses. Across all measures, robust differences between go and no-go trials were found, supporting construct validity. All behavioral and kinematic measures demonstrated moderate-to-good test-retest reliability (ICCs ranging from .59 to .85), establishing the paradigm's suitability for cross-sectional and longitudinal research targeting inhibitory control.
procedure: Each session began with two practice blocks (18 trials each: block 1 go-only, block 2 MIXED go/no-go — 14 go / 4 no-go, driven by go_nogo_prac.xlsx; the preprint §2.3 describes block 2 as no-go-only, which the data contradicts in all 50 sessions). The main experiment consisted of 15 blocks arranged as repeated sequences of three blocks: one go-only block (18 trials) followed by two mixed go/no-go blocks (60 trials each; 80% go, 20% no-go), repeated four times, plus a final go-only block for symmetrical design (5 go-only + 8 mixed blocks). Each trial started with a 500 ms fixation cross, then a blue start box appeared at screen bottom center. Participants positioned and held the cursor in the start box for 500 ms (mouse movement initiation requirement). The box turned black, the response box appeared in the upper-right quadrant, and the stimulus digit appeared only after the cursor crossed a vertical threshold 100 pixels above the start position. On go trials, participants clicked in the response box within 1500 ms. On no-go trials, participants withheld response. A variable ITI (0.5–1.0 s) followed, during which the cursor was not visible.
trial_structure: Trial onset: 500 ms fixation → start box (blue) → participant holds cursor for 500 ms → start box turns black → response box appears → stimulus appears after cursor crosses threshold → go: click within response box within 1500 ms deadline; no-go: withhold click → ITI (0.5–1.0 s, cursor hidden). Digits 1 and 9 = no-go (6 presentations each per mixed block); digits 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8 = go (8 each per mixed block). Trial order within mixed blocks pseudorandomized with constraints on go/no-go transitions.
design: Within-subjects, repeated-measures. Two sessions per participant separated by approximately one week (test-retest design). Two trial types (go, no-go) within each block. Mixed blocks: 80% go, 20% no-go. Five go-only blocks and eight mixed blocks per session.

implementations.note: Builder-generated experiment (go_nogo_dm.py) plus its condition tables, stimulus images and German instruction deck. The .psyexp / _lastrun.py pair must stay together.

Hand-written single-file re-implementation (MT_paradigm_short.py) plus a browser demo (MT_demo.html). Same geometry, timings and scoring rules as go_nogo_dm.py, verified line by line; it is a shorter SCRIPT, not a shortened paradigm.

timing.iti_duration_note: Six discrete steps drawn with random.choice (go_nogo_dm.py 513, 2437), not a continuous range.

outcome_measures.label: Accuracy
outcome_measures.description: Go: first left click inside the response box, exactly one click, no other button. No-go: a validated stop with no button press.

outcome_measures.label: Reaction Time
outcome_measures.description: Go: latency from stimulus onset to the correct click. No-go: stopping latency (inhibition latency), 0 where no movement was initiated.

outcome_measures.label: Path Length
outcome_measures.description: Total cursor distance travelled over the trial epoch.

outcome_measures.label: Mean Velocity
outcome_measures.description: Path length divided by movement duration.

derivation.description: Stage 1 projects the raw PsychoPy export onto the analysis column set and drops the four leading and one trailing non-trial rows. Stage 2 ports 1__compute_stopping.R: parses trajectory arrays, extracts left-button clicks inside the target box, detects no-go stopping by velocity threshold with sustained-stillness verification, scores accuracy and combined RT. Stage 3 ports 3__Kinematics.R: path length, mean velocity, mean acceleration over the trial epoch, time-weighted. Stage 4 emits per-outcome files restricted to the analysed subset.
derivation.analysed_subset: block_type == 'go_nogo' — the eight mixed blocks of 60 trials, 480 per session. Practice and go-only blocks stay in bids_data but are excluded from the outcome files, matching go_nogo_compiledData.csv (23,040 rows = 48 sessions x 480).
derivation.parameter_hazard: post_still_s (0.25) sizes the post-stop stillness CHECK in the stopping script. kinematics_epoch_tail_s (0.150) sizes the no-go kinematics WINDOW; 3__Kinematics.R names its own constant POST_STILL_SEC, which is NOT the same quantity. Confusing them inflates every no-go duration by 100 ms and depresses no-go velocity and acceleration by ~15%, while leaving path length, all go measures and ALL ICCs correct — reliability checks alone cannot detect it.
derivation.exclusions: Trials with unparseable trajectory arrays are scored n/a, never 0 — a parse failure must not inflate accuracy. Outcome files are NOT outlier-trimmed; the paper's ±2.5 SD cell-wise trim is applied at analysis time by code/reproduce_paper_MT.py.
derivation.verified: 2026-08 by convert_MT.py + reproduce_paper_MT.py: reproduced the preprint's N (23), outlier rate (2.11% vs 2.1%), error rates, RTs, path length, no-go velocity and acceleration, and all ten ICCs with confidence intervals. Residual: go mean velocity +1.31% and go mean acceleration +1.34%, with go path length exact.

The dashboard card shows 0.63 for ACCBIN, the MEAN of the go (0.68) and no-go (0.59) ICCs. MT is the only project whose reliability_metrics are keyed by trial type (go, nogo) rather than by a single condition, so it is the only one whose card value is an average across conditions. 0.63 corresponds to no figure in the preprint, which reports go and no-go separately (.75 and .59 for error rate). Decide whether the card should show the mean, the primary trial type, or both. Note also that the card's go value (0.68) differs from reproduce_paper_MT.py's (0.75) because the outcome files are not outlier-trimmed.

_role_decision: PI decision 2026-08: ACCBIN primary, RT secondary, declared explicitly via the `role` keys. Follows the abstract's split into standard behavioural measures and three kinematic features, and matches the ACCBIN/RT pairing in APPL and OLM. Recorded tension: no-go accuracy has the weakest reliability of all ten measures (ICC .59), so the primary outcome is the least reliable one. Polarity note: ACCBIN is accuracy (higher is better); the paper reports error rate. ICC(3,1) is unchanged by x -> 1-x, so reliability figures stay directly comparable.
_file_placement_rule: PI rule 2026-08: paradigm/ holds every file needed to RUN the paradigm — scripts, condition tables, stimulus images and the instruction deck (instructions_de.pptx). literature/ holds only the PDF publications and related papers. This overrides MT_migration_plan.md and the earlier note in Agent/notes/MT.md, both of which sent instructions_de.pptx to literature/.
